result.topic_en: The page holds four notes: the aim and the method (method is not an end in itself); a criticism of Zolotarev's 1880 paper on complex numbers with a counterexample; a problem of approximately counting integer solutions of a linear Diophantine inequality; and an analogy between irrational numbers and ideal numbers as extensions of the number concept.

Die Arbeit von Zolotaref „über complexe Zahlen“ in Liouville's
Journal S. III Bd 6 1880 ist in ihren wesent-
lichen Kern Unsinn. Man betrachte das Beispiel
$F = V^m - pV + p^2$, wo $V$ eine ganze ganzzahlige Function von
$x$ ist, welche irreducibel ist mod[-p-]ulo der Primzahl $p$. Nun
ist
$V^{2m-1} = (V - V^{m-1} - p)p^2 + (V^{m-1} + p)(V^m - pV + p^2)$
also laut der Zolotarefschen Definition durch keine Potenz
der idealen Primzahl $(p, V)$ teilbar. Dadurch wird alles
weitere falsch.

items.english: Zolotarev's paper 'on complex numbers' in Liouville's Journal, Series III, Vol. 6, 1880, is nonsense in its essential core.

items.english: Thus, according to Zolotarev's definition, it is divisible by no power of the ideal prime (p, V). This makes everything further false.
